children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Tuesday.

Russia attacked Ukraine's port infrastructure and a border crossing with Romania in the southern Black Sea region of Odesa, Ukrainian officials said.

Turkey said on Monday that it had prepared a plan for the safe passage of grain via the Black Sea. However, Moscow believes a moratorium on attacks in the Black Sea will not bring the prospect of a peaceful resolution to the war any closer, Interfax reported.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last up 4-1/2 cents at $7.78-1/2 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last up 3 cents at $8.41 a bushel, and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last up 3-3/4 cents at $7.66-3/4 a bushel.
CBOT and K.C. futures set contract highs.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture kept its good-to-excellent rating for the nation's corn crop unchanged at 57% in a weekly report on Monday. That was down from 69% a year ago.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 1 cent at $5.36-3/4 per bushel. The contract earlier set a high of $5.43-3/4.

Exporters sold 136,000 metric tons of U.S. soybeans to China, the USDA said.
Uncertainty over U.S. yield potential supported prices after the USDA lowered its condition rating for the nation's soybean crop on Monday.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last up 12-1/2 cents at $13.00-1/2 per bushel. The market set contract highs.
